title: South Africa's digital access is widespread but mobile-first and sharply uneven across provinces
source_unit: Statistics South Africa, General Household Survey 2025
geography: South Africa; private households across all nine provinces and residents in workers' hostels

observations.period: 2010-2025; household internet access by location and device

denominator.unit: households in the GHS 2025 public-use household file; national estimates are benchmarked household survey estimates

internet_access_anywhere_2010.unit: percent of households with internet access at any location

internet_access_anywhere_2025.unit: percent of households with internet access at any location

fixed_home_internet_2025.unit: percent of households with fixed internet access at home

mobile_internet_2025.unit: percent of households with internet access through mobile devices

mechanism.value: Internet access has become widespread mainly through mobile connectivity, while fixed home access remains a minority condition; digital cultural and consumer participation therefore rests on different quality, cost, privacy, and reliability conditions than a binary online/offline measure reveals

observations.method: Statistics South Africa annual household survey with national time-series indicators; access includes home, work, study, internet café, public hotspot, library, and other locations.
observations.uncertainty: The measure records household access or use at one or more locations, not individual frequency, bandwidth, affordability, data expenditure, device quality, or cultural use.
observations.subgroup: Private households across South Africa's nine provinces and residents in workers' hostels; institutional and military collective quarters are excluded.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mobile-first access may be sufficient for some cultural and consumer activities, and the survey cannot establish that fixed access produces better outcomes for every use.

denominator.unit: households in the GHS 2025 public-use household file; provincial estimates are weighted household survey estimates

western_cape_any_internet.unit: percent of households with any internet access

eastern_cape_any_internet.unit: percent of households with any internet access

western_cape_fixed_home_internet.unit: percent of households with fixed internet at home

limpopo_fixed_home_internet.unit: percent of households with fixed internet at home

public_wifi_national.unit: percent of households reporting public Wi-Fi access

mechanism.value: National digital reach conceals a provincial infrastructure gradient: both basic connectivity and the more stable fixed-home layer are concentrated unevenly, shaping the reliability and privacy of downstream cultural, social, and consumer use

observations.method: GHS 2025 provincial table for internet access by type; provincial percentages are weighted household estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Province is an aggregate place marker and does not isolate network supply, income, urbanicity, electricity reliability, device ownership, or data prices.
observations.subgroup: Households in Western Cape, Eastern Cape, Limpopo, and all other South African provinces.
observations.counterinterpretation: High mobile access can partially compensate for low fixed access, while fixed-home differences may reflect household choice as well as infrastructure and affordability.

denominator.unit: households in the GHS 2025 public-use household file; national weighted household estimates

single_person_households.unit: percent of households consisting of one person

female_headed_households.unit: percent of households headed by a woman

food_access_inadequate_or_severely_inade.unit: percent of households reporting inadequate or severely inadequate food access

social_grant_recipient_individuals.unit: percent of individuals benefiting from social grants

mechanism.value: Digital access sits inside highly differentiated household structures and material constraints; connectivity can expand while food insecurity, grant dependence, and household isolation continue to shape what digital or cultural consumption is affordable and meaningful

observations.method: GHS 2025 household structure, food-access, and social-grant indicators from the national survey release; the measures describe different denominators and should not be read as one causal chain.
observations.uncertainty: These aggregate indicators do not identify individual welfare trajectories, spending substitution, social connection quality, or causal effects of household structure or grants on digital or cultural use.
observations.subgroup: South African households and individuals represented by the GHS 2025 national estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Single-person households can have greater autonomy, grants can protect consumption, and food-access measures may fluctuate seasonally; none automatically implies reduced cultural participation.

related_sources.claim: Statistics South Africa publication page identifies the GHS 2025 release, release date, main publication, key findings, and downloadable tables.
Public metadata documents the GHS 2025 target population, sampling design, weighting, and public-use household file with 20,095 cases.

boundary: This record adds South African evidence on mobile-first digital access, provincial infrastructure inequality, household structure, food access, and social-grant coverage. It does not measure cultural participation, digital frequency, data prices, device quality, platform use, or causal household welfare effects.
